Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 3097 of 2023
Applicant :- Shailendra Kumar Singh
Opposite Party :- Central Bureau Of Investigation Anti Corruption Branch Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Himanshu Hemant Gupta
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Anurag Kumar Singh
Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
Paper book of this case has been placed before this Court under the orders of Hon'ble The Chief
Justice dated 01.04.2024.

1. Heard Shri Himanshu Hemant Gupta, learned counsel for the applicant, Shri Akhilendra Singh,
Advocate holding brief of Shri Anurag Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the respondent- CBI, and perused the record.
2.

This application has been moved by the applicant- Shailendra Kumar Singh for grant of anticipatory bail in Session Case No.491 of 2023, arising out of RC0062011A0007, under Sections 120-B, 420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C. and Section 13(2) read with Section 13(1)(d) P.C. Act lodged at Police Station CBI/ACB, Lucknow.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that it is a case of false implication.

sentences.text:
It is further submitted that the FIR of this case has been registered by the CBI on 13.04.2011 against named accused persons and some unknown officers/officials of district industries centre, district Chandauli and officers/officials of northern coal fields limited alleging that certain illegalities have been committed in supplying coal by the officers/officials of northern coal fields limited and a huge amount has been misappropriated in connivance with the officers/officials of district industries centre.
4.

It is further submitted that during the course of investigation the role of the applicant is alleged to the tune that he is the owner of M/s Rajlaxmi Enterprises and during the year 2010-2011 sale of about 617.76 metric ton of SSF and 378.70 metric tons of undersized coal was shown to have been made to the company of the applicant by M/s Shree Ram Fuels Pvt. Ltd. through 42 and 24 truck-loads.

It is vehemently submitted that without there being any sufficient evidence/material the charge-sheet had been submitted by the CBI and thereafter the Directorate of Enforcement has started investigation in the matter.

It is further submitted that in the year 2007 the Ministry of Coal had come with a new coal distribution policy and fuel supply agreements, which were entered into between the NCL and coal companies and the said agreements were binding and enforceable qua the parties and there was a specific penalty clause under these agreements and when the penalty clause was provided in the contract itself, initiation of criminal proceedings is bad and, therefore,
any alleged breach of the agreement committed by the M/s Shree Ram Fuels Pvt. Ltd. cannot be a criminal offence and initiation of any criminal proceeding on such breach of agreement is a sheer abuse of process of the law.

5. It is also submitted that the primary allegations against the applicant is to the tune that he was purchaser of coal from M/s Shree Ram Fuels Pvt. Ltd. and, therefore, the relevant provisions of sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 IPC and sections 13(2) read with Sections 13(1)(d) P.C. Act could only be attracted against the director of M/s Shree Ram Fuels Pvt. Ltd. and the DIC officials as the applicant was only the bona fide purchaser of coal from M/s Shree Ram Fuels Pvt. Ltd. and also he was not a party to the said agreements and in fact he was not having any knowledge of the said agreements or any of their condition at that point of time.

It is further submitted that the applicant after filing of the charge-sheet had approached this Court by filing a petition under Section 482 CrPC No. 4553 of 2012 and vide order dated 19.10.2012 were granted interim order and the said petition was connected with a bunch of petitions and the interim order dated 19.10.2012 was extended from time to time and was confirmed by the Court vide order dated 24.02.2015 and the matter was referred to the division bench of this court.
It is further submitted that vide another order dated 14.08.2019 the petition under Section 482 CrPC No. 4553 of 2012 was dismissed.

6. It is vehemently submitted that during the course of investigation the applicant has cooperated in the investigation and had remained present before the investigating officer as and when his presence was required and since the charge-sheet has been submitted, the applicant would also cooperate in the trial as he has cooperated in the investigation.

It is also submitted that co-accused persons, namely, Ravindra Aggarwal and Gajraj Kunwar Jain have been granted anticipatory bail vide orders passed in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Nos. 857 of 2023 and 1696 of 2023 and one of the co-accused person- Ramji Singh has also been granted anticipatory bail vide order passed in Shailendra Kumar Singh vs Central Bureau Of Investigation Anti ...

It is further submitted that since the applicant has not been arrested by the investigating agency and he has cooperated in the investigation, the interim protection order was granted in his favour, which he has not misused, the facility of anticipatory bail be provided to him.

It is next submitted that identically placed co-accused person, namely, Aftab Ahmad and Mohammad Zakariya have also been granted the facility of anticipatory bail, vide order dated 15.02.2024 passed in CRIMINAL MISC ANTICIPATORY BAIL APPLICATION U/S 438 CR.P.C. No. - 3109 of 2023.

7. Shri Akhilednra Singh, learned counsel representing the C.B.I. opposes the prayer of the applicant for grant of anticipatory bail but could not dispute the fact that the applicant has cooperated in the investigation, he was not named in the FIR and also that many other co-accused persons have been granted anticipatory bail.
8.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is reflected that the applicant has cooperated in the investigation throughout and the charge-sheet has been filed without making his arrest.
The applicant is not named in the FIR.
It is also surfaced that this matter remained pending before this Court in various jurisdictions and ultimately the trial started before the trial Court.

The applicant on approaching this Court were granted interim protection order dated 22.12.2023 subject to certain conditions and nothing has been brought before this Court which may suggest that the applicant has violated any of the conditions under which his personal liberty was protected.

Thus, having regard to all the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping an eye on the specific circumstance that during the course of investigation the applicant was not arrested by the investigating agency, the facility of anticipatory bail may safely be extended to him on merits as well as on principle of parity as various co-accused persons, including Ramji Singh and Aftab Ahmad and Mohammad Zakariya have been granted the facility of anticipatory bail.
9. Thus, the instant anticipatory bail application moved on behalf of the applicant- Shailendra Kumar Singh is allowed and the interim protection order dated 22.12.2023 is made absolute.

It is provided that in the event of arrest of the applicant under any process of the trial Court or on his appearance/surrender before the trial Court within 20 days from today i.e. till 02.06.2024,
whichever is earlier, he shall be released forthwith on anticipatory bail on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 50,000/- and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court,
subject to the following conditions:-
(i). The applicant, if not arrested earlier, shall appear before the trial court within 20 days from today i.e. till 02.06.2024 and cooperate in the trial and shall not seek any adjournment when the prosecution witness would be in attendance.
(ii). In case of further investigation or re-investigation the applicant shall cooperate in the investigation and make himself available as and when required by the Investigating officer of the case, even for the recovery of any fact.
(iii).
The applicant shall not make any attempt to influence the prosecution witnesses and will also not commit any crime during his release on anticipatory bail.

(v). The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
10.
The personal bond as well as surety bonds, if filed by the applicant and are sufficient in the opinion of the trial Court, the applicant no need to file the same again.

11. If in the opinion of the trial court default of any of the condition placed above is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and shall proceed against him/her in accordance with law.
12. It is clarified that all the observations contained in this order are only for disposal of this anticipatory bail application and shall not affect the trial proceedings in any manner.
